assertions.name: pairwise_backbone_recovers_coulomb_mirror_split
assertions.source: deuteron-pinned pairwise backbone B_2=B(D)·C(A,2): the ³H−³He residual difference 0.7638 MeV ≈ AME mirror split 0.7638 (equal BY CONSTRUCTION — the A=3 backbone B_2=B(D)·C(3,2) is identical for ³H/³He and cancels; verified to <1e-6 on floats) ⇒ M_n=C(A,n) inherits the Coulomb charge structure; the pairwise 2-body count holds with zero extra parameters. M_3/M_4 weights open.

description: Per-order sub-link count M_n(K)=C(A,n) for the body-order coordination tower (qou-v0yw, sharpened by #3582). The n=2 pairwise backbone B_2=B(D)·C(A,2) is pinned by the SINGLE deuteron datum (a_D^(2)=1, C(2,2)=1) and reproduces A=3 binding to a small ~1–2 MeV M_3 residual; the ³H−³He residual difference EQUALS the Coulomb mirror split (recovering #3564/#3570); ⁴He residual is the magic 4-body. So M_n=C(A,n) fits the 2-body backbone with zero extra parameters; the M_3/M_4 weights + large-A saturation stay open. Scope-(a), no per-isotope fit.
